While judging pizza sounds like a dream job, the process is rigorous. The awards rely on nearly 1,000 anonymous inspectors worldwide with zero ties to the restaurants they judge. Every contender is visited twice, with judges scoring the experience from dough structure and ingredient sourcing to service and hospitality. It takes a lot more than a good crust to win, making this homegrown victory all the more impressive.
Last year, Napoli on the Road placed fifth at the same World Awards, well behind the reigning champion, New York’s Una Pizza Napoletana, which had held the world’s top spot for two years running. This year, Pascarella didn’t just climb the rankings but knocked the champion off the top spot completely.
![Michele Pascarella of Napoli on the Road](https://media.timeout.com/images/106447867/image.webp) 
This is just the latest trophy in a relentless run of accolades for Pascarella. He was crowned the world’s best pizza chef back in 2023, and his restaurant has topped the separate 50 Top Pizza Europa awards for three consecutive years from 2024 to 2026, with his signature pizza, Ricordi d’Infanzia, winning Pizza of the Year at the 2025 edition of those same Europa awards.
Pascarella moved to the UK from Maddaloni, near Naples, at just 19. He started Napoli on the Road in 2016 as a three-wheeled Piaggio Ape van fitted with a wood-fired oven, slinging pizzas at farmers’ markets and outdoor events across London long before the business ever had chairs and tables. The operation has since grown into bricks-and-mortar restaurants in Chiswick and Richmond, with a third site opening in Soho back in February, home to Pascarella’s pizza tasting menu drawing on his childhood and Italian heritage.
And if Italian food is on the brain, the UK’s ‘biggest’ Italian restaurant is opening in London.

summary: Napoli on the Road in Chiswick, London, has been named the World's Best Pizzeria at the 50 Top Pizza World Awards in Naples. Founded by chef Michele Pascarella, the restaurant dethroned New York's Una Pizza Napoletana, which had previously held the top spot for two years. The victory follows a rigorous judging process involving nearly 1,000 anonymous inspectors evaluating aspects such as dough structure, ingredients, and service.
key_points: Napoli on the Road in Chiswick, London, was named the World's Best Pizzeria.
The restaurant is founded by chef Michele Pascarella.
The award was presented at the 50 Top Pizza World Awards ceremony in Naples.
The restaurant surpassed last year's reigning champion, New York's Una Pizza Napoletana.
Pascarella started the business in 2016 as a three-wheeled van before expanding to physical restaurants.

title: Million Dollar Quartet review – London transfer for the jukebox extravaganza
author: Hang Yuen
content:
![MDQ 300x200](https://www.whatsonstage.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/08/MDQ-300x200-1.png?w=300) 
The production, directed by Jonathan O’Boyle, will also be touring until July 2027
Million Dollar Quartet arrives with an irresistible proposition: live music, 23 songs and four figures at the birth of rock ’n’ roll. At the Arts at Marble Arch, the set initially promises a time machine to the 1950s. A large proscenium frame lined with warm marquee bulbs surrounds a black-and-white chequerboard floor, while dark wood panelling, records, photographs and vintage memorabilia create a cosy music-room-meets-retro-TV-studio aesthetic. Guitars, double bass, drums and piano hug the walls. A show-within-a-show framed almost like an old television screen.
The musicians certainly deliver. Darren Day’s enterprising producer Sam Phillips establishes the evening with warmth and easy command. When an audience member calls out, his quick response becomes an effective piece of spontaneous interaction. Joe Bence’s Jerry Lee Lewis is immediately captivating, particularly in his formidable keyboard playing. Across the company, the musicianship is technically impressive.
The lighting (by Alex Musgrave) is perhaps the production’s strongest creative element. Narrow neon beams, amber light bars and shifting colours create an atmospheric interplay between warm nostalgia and sharper stage illumination. The red-and-white palette of Jenay Naima’s Dyanne and Christopher Erasmus’ Johnny Cash’s red, orange and blue solo lighting are especially effective.
Cash’s “I Walk the Line” is a highlight. Its dynamic arc, driven by continual key modulations and shifting vocal registers across five verses, showcases the performers’ technical precision. The movement between soft and stronger lighting complements the musical progression, creating an effect that is as visually compelling as it is aurally satisfying. Beyond this, Naima’s “Fever”, delivered with a soft, magnetic vocal quality against warm yellow light, is one of the evening’s most beautifully integrated moments.
The venue has its flaws: incessant sirens can pull you away from the nostalgia. The show itself is also less than perfect: by the seventh song, the dramatic structure begins to show its limitations: music, scene, speech, music, scene, speech. The formula becomes increasingly predictable. The performers remain engaging, but the momentum repeatedly stalls.
The staging compounds the problem. Limited space occasionally forces actors to turn their backs to the audience, while (half) frozen performers in the background attempt to establish another location. The intention is clear; the theatrical solution is awkward. More inventive use of space could create separation without compromising the performers’ relationship with the audience.
The script is similarly overburdened. Religion, sin, marriage and sexual morality, particularly through Jerry Lee’s extended passages, sometimes generate awkward silence rather than dramatic tension. A racially offensive historical phrase also feels unnecessary when it neither advances the plot nor substantially deepens character.
The production works best when it embraces itself as an exuberant celebration of 1950s music: joyful, nostalgic and irresistible, but attempts to add greater historical or dramatic weight instead expose thin characterisation, particularly for Elvis Presley and Johnny Cash.
Yet the finale finally finds its emotional register. A Polaroid captures the four musicians together as Sam reflects on their first and last shared moment. Coral sunset beams and Sam’s reflection in the mirror create a beautiful sense of circularity as he takes one final look around the studio. The talent is undeniable, the musicians play brilliantly and the lighting frequently shines.
summary: The London transfer of "Million Dollar Quartet" at the Arts at Marble Arch offers an energetic jukebox musical featuring 23 live rock 'n' roll songs and strong musicianship. While the production boasts impressive lighting, standout musical numbers, and a moving finale, it suffers from a predictable dramatic formula, spatial limitations, and an overburdened script. Ultimately, the show shines brightest as a joyful celebration of 1950s music rather than when attempting deeper historical or dramatic weight.
key_points: The production features technically impressive musicianship, standout performances, and atmospheric lighting by Alex Musgrave.
Performances of songs like Johnny Cash's "I Walk the Line" and Jenay Naima's "Fever" are notable highlights of the evening.
The show's dramatic structure becomes predictable due to a repetitive music-scene-speech formula and spatial staging constraints.
Attempts to add historical and dramatic weight expose thin characterisation and awkward script elements.
The production succeeds best as an exuberant, nostalgic celebration of 1950s music, anchored by a poignant finale.

title: This pretty, leafy neighbourhood is the coolest in London, according to Time Out
author: Ed Cunningham
content:
[title]
London is crammed with neighbourhoods that, in some way or other, you might consider ‘cool’. Dalston’s non-stop vibes, Soho’s decades-established charisma, Peckham’s rich cultural blend, Notting Hill’s sleek bistros, Camden’s punks and skateboarders… whatever your definition of cool, London’s got it.
It’s no surprise, therefore, that part of the capital featured in Time Out’s 2026 ranking of the coolest neighbourhoods in the world. This year’s list includes places nominated by Time Out’s global network of travel experts, who weighed in with top spots to eat, drink, shop and chill out right now. The final order was decided by a panel of Time Out editors.
Named the coolest neighbourhood in London this year was, drum roll please… Newington Green. The leafy, chic area, which is sandwiched between Islington and Hackney, placed 33rd in the global list.
![Newington Green](https://media.timeout.com/images/106447032/image.webp) 
Newington Green was nominated by Time Out UK editor-in-chief Joe Mackertich. He said:
‘Yes, Newington Green’s winsome appeal isn’t new. It’s been “very nice” there for a while now. What is inarguable though, is that the area has achieved a kind of critical mass of niceness.’
Joe reckoned that the area contains so many top cafés, pubs, indie food shops and critically-adored restaurants that it’s currently the best place to eat and drink in London.
![All Greens, Newington Green](https://media.timeout.com/images/106447013/image.webp) 
And Newington Green isn’t just a pretty face with great grub: it’s also, as Joe explains, ‘a neighbourhood with centuries of history and tons of community spirit’. Once a major hub for London’s Turkish and Cypriot immigrant population, N16 also boasts the Newington Green Meeting House, which has been a home for progressive causes for over 300 years.
Where to start if you’re visiting Newington Green? Well, Joe picks out trendy gastropub The Golden Tooth, butcher-nightclub Stella’s, posh bakery Jolene, Turkish food joints Sariyer Balik and 01 Adana, top boozer the Army & Navy, wine bar Cadet, fresh pizza spot Bar Etna and the legendary Mildmay Club. You can peruse a gallery of Newington Green’s chicest spots here.
![Mildmay Club, Newington Green](https://media.timeout.com/images/106447005/image.webp) 
2026 marks the the ninth edition of Time Out’s coolest neighbourhoods in the world. Previous London areas that have made the cut include Peckham (2018-19), Soho (2020), Dalston (2021), Walthamstow (2022), King’s Cross (2023), Leyton (2024) and Camberwell (2026).
Crowned the coolest neighbourhood in the world this year was Seoul’s Jongno 3-ga, followed by Rabat’s L’Ocean District and Neos Kosmos in Athens. Two other communities in the UK made the cut: Glasgow’s Govanhill (in fifth) and Belfast’s Cathedral Quarter (24)
Get the latest and greatest from the Big Smoke – from news and reviews to events and trends. Just follow our Time Out London WhatsApp channel.
Stay in the loop: sign up to our free Time Out London newsletter for the best of the city, straight to your inbox.
summary: Time Out has named Newington Green as the coolest neighbourhood in London for 2026, ranking it 33rd on their global list. Located between Islington and Hackney, the leafy area was praised for its abundance of top cafés, pubs, restaurants, and centuries of history with strong community spirit. Time Out's editor-in-chief highlighted local spots such as The Golden Tooth, Jolene, and the historic Mildmay Club.
key_points: Newington Green was named London's coolest neighbourhood by Time Out for 2026 and ranked 33rd globally.
The area was recognized for achieving a critical mass of great places to eat, drink, and shop.
Newington Green features a rich history, community spirit, and landmarks like the Newington Green Meeting House and Mildmay Club.
Other global locations, such as Seoul's Jongno 3-ga, topped the overall world ranking.

title: ‘Putney pusher’ suspect found dead
author: Alex Ross
content:
The prime suspect in the notorious “Putney pusher” case has been found dead at his home in west London.
Banker Nicholas Brandram, 44, was arrested on suspicion of attempted grievous bodily harm following a decade-long manhunt after a woman, who has never been named, was shoved into the path of a bus on Putney Bridge in 2017.
On Tuesday, Mr Brandram, a descendant of Queen Victoria, was found dead at his property in Chiswick. The Met Police said the death of a 44-year-old man was being treated as “unexpected”, and was not believed to be suspicious.
In a statement, the force said: “At 19:12hrs on Tuesday, 15 September officers and the London Ambulance Service attended an address in Chiswick, Hounslow, after a man was found unresponsive inside a property. Sadly, a 44-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene. His next-of-kin have been informed.”
![Nicholas Brandram pictured in 2013](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/09/16/15/26/nicholas-brandram-new.jpeg)
The force will prepare a file for the coroner in due course, a spokesperson said.
CCTV of the incident on Putney Bridge on 5 May 2017 showed a jogger forcefully shoving the female pedestrian with both of his hands into the path of a double-decker bus. Around 15 minutes later, he passed her as she was receiving help on the bridge and ignored her calls for him to stop.
The woman, who was 33 at the time, sustained a few minor injuries.
![CCTV captured the notorious “Putney pusher” following the incident in 2017](https://static.independent.co.uk/2024/04/10/11/putney%20pusher%201.jpg)
The suspect was described by the Met Police as in his early to mid-30s, with short brown hair and a stocky build. He was wearing dark blue shorts, trainers and a grey T-shirt.
At the time, police interviewed more than 50 men and arrested three suspects, but the case was closed in 2018, and no one was ever charged.
But on 15 June, Mr Brandram was arrested at his home in connection with the case. The force then said: “A 44-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted grievous bodily harm. The arrest relates to an incident on May 5, 2017, where a woman was pushed into the path of a bus on Putney Bridge in Putney.”
Last week, the force announced the suspect had been released under investigation.
Mr Brandram was a senior relationship manager HSBC Private Bank, according to an interview he did with Citywealth earlier this year.
The Sun reported that he was a former British Army Captain who served in Iraq, Bosnia and Afghanistan. He was awarded a Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal at the time of her celebrations to mark 60 years on the throne in 2012.
Mr Brandram was a grandson of Princess Katherine of Greeceand Denmark, who was the great-granddaughter of Queen Victoria.
summary: Nicholas Brandram, the prime suspect in the 2017 "Putney pusher" case, has been found dead at his home in west London at the age of 44. Brandram was arrested in June on suspicion of attempted grievous bodily harm after a woman was shoved into the path of a bus on Putney Bridge, though the case had previously been closed without charges in 2018. The Metropolitan Police stated that his death is being treated as unexpected but not suspicious.
key_points: Nicholas Brandram was found dead at his Chiswick property on Tuesday.
He was the prime suspect in the 2017 Putney Bridge bus-shoving incident.
Police stated his death was unexpected and not believed to be suspicious.
No one was ever formally charged in connection with the original 2017 case.

title: Biker flown to London hospital after crash with car on A2
author: Louis Walker
content:
UK regional news website of the year
A biker has been airlifted to a London hospital after a crash with a car.
Traffic was halted in both directions on the A2 in Gravesend following the incident on the London-bound carriageway near the A227 Wrotham Road at around 7.20am.
A spokesperson for the ambulance service said: “Crews attended the scene and assessed and treated the driver of the motorbike for injuries, including to their wrist.
“We were joined by The Air Ambulance Charity, Kent Surrey Sussex and the patient was airlifted to King’s College Hospital for further medical treatment.”
At its peak, there were delays of more than an hour on the route while emergency services were at the scene.
The London-bound carriageway was shut at around 7.20am, but all lanes have since reopened.
The coast-bound side was closed for about 20 minutes to allow the air ambulance to land, but has also since reopened.
Drivers faced lengthy queues throughout the morning rush-hour, but delays have now cleared.
summary: A motorcyclist was airlifted to a London hospital following a collision with a car on the A2 in Gravesend. The incident caused traffic to be halted in both directions during the morning rush-hour, resulting in delays of over an hour. Emergency services responded to the scene, and all lanes have since reopened.
key_points: A biker and a car crashed on the London-bound carriageway of the A2 in Gravesend.
The motorcyclist sustained injuries, including to the wrist, and was airlifted to King's College Hospital.
Traffic was halted in both directions, causing delays of more than an hour during the morning rush-hour.
Emergency services responded to the scene, and all lanes on both sides of the road have since reopened.

title: London council tax hammerblow as borough set to nearly double bills in record rise
author: Michael Howie; Rachael Burford
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Battersea Park in Wandsworth](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/16/6/52/GettyImages-2217219679.jpeg?trim=0,47,0,47&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
The record increase - a staggering 94% rise - will take the Tory minority-run borough from having the lowest council tax in the country to around average levels.
The south London council, which announced the move on Tuesday night following what it called a “comprehensive” spending review.
It blamed the Labour government’s Fair Funding reforms - which will see spending shifted from London to the North - for reducing Wandsworth’s funding by £84million a year.
The council said that cut was equivalent to the borough’s total combined annual spending on parks, libraries, leisure centres, bin collection and street cleaning.
Wandsworth Council’s deputy leader Peter Graham, who is cabinet member for finance, said it did not take the decision to impose a record council tax rise lightly.
He said: “We promised that we’d be honest with residents.
“Council tax will need to rise unless Government thinks again. And it must think again.
“We do not want to do this, and we do not take this decision lightly, but the scale of the financial pressure facing Wandsworth means additional income is now needed to protect the services people rely on.
“Residents should not be left to carry the cost of an unfair funding system. That is why we are fighting hard at the heart of Government for a fairer deal for Wandsworth, and why we have made a clear case ahead of the Autumn Budget that our borough should not be punished for running efficient services and keeping council tax low.
“Our message to residents is clear: we are on your side, we are making your case, and we will keep fighting for the funding Wandsworth deserves.”
Read More
With around 340,000 residents, Wandsworth is one of the capital’s most populous boroughs. It was the Conservative’s flagship London borough for decades, having been under Tory control from 1978 to 2022, when Labour took over.
summary: Wandsworth Council has announced a record 94% increase in council tax following a spending review, moving the borough from having the lowest council tax in the country to near-average levels. The Tory minority-run south London council blamed the Labour government's Fair Funding reforms, which it says will reduce its funding by £84 million a year. Deputy leader Peter Graham stated that the hike is necessary to protect essential services unless the government reconsiders the funding system.
key_points: Wandsworth Council announced a record 94% increase in council tax.
The borough previously had the lowest council tax in the country.
The council blamed a £84 million annual funding reduction resulting from the Labour government's Fair Funding reforms.
The funding cut is equivalent to the borough's combined spending on parks, libraries, leisure centres, bin collection, and street cleaning.
Wandsworth has around 340,000 residents and is one of London's most populous boroughs.

title: Train services cancelled on major route due to trespassers
author: Hallie Taylor
content:
Train services to Norwich were being cancelled or delayed due to trespassers blocking the tracks.
Trespassers were on the tracks at Ipswich, causing all lines to be blocked.
Greater Anglia services between Norwich and London were being cancelled or delayed as a result.
British Transport Police were on the scene, and services are expected to be disrupted until around 11.30am today.
Other affected routes include Ipswich to Felixstowe, Lowestoft, Cambridge and Peterborough.
Trains were unable to depart or arrive at Ipswich at present and Greater Anglia has advised passengers to prepare for delays.
A spokesman for Greater Anglia said: "The British Transport Police is on site at Ipswich because of a trespasser on the tracks.
"Until the person and all personnel are clear of the track, lines are currently blocked for safety reasons."
The following services have been disrupted: the 8am, 8.30am, and 9am services from London Liverpool Street to Norwich, due at 9.48am, 10.18am and 10.47am, respectively.
The 8.30am, 9am, 9.30am, and 10.30am services from Norwich to London Liverpool Street have also been affected.
The company has arranged for Greater Anglia tickets to be accepted on several local bus services as an alternative travel option.
This includes First buses 64, 75, 77, 88, and P&R 800, and Central Connect buses 74, 75, 82, and 70.
Greater Anglia emphasised the dangers of trespassing on railway lines, which is illegal and can result in a £1,000 fine.
Train services have returned to normal.
summary: Train services between Norwich and London, as well as several other routes, were disrupted due to trespassers on the tracks at Ipswich. British Transport Police responded to the scene, leading to blocked lines and widespread cancellations or delays. Greater Anglia advised passengers of the delays and arranged for tickets to be accepted on alternative local bus services.
key_points: Trespassers on the tracks at Ipswich caused significant train cancellations and delays.
British Transport Police attended the scene to clear the area for safety.
Affected routes included services between Norwich, London, Felixstowe, Lowestoft, Cambridge, and Peterborough.
Greater Anglia accepted rail tickets on multiple local bus services as an alternative.
Train services have since returned to normal.

title: London schools crisis: Ministers told to fix 'traumatic' closures for pupils
author: Kumail Jaffer
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![School closures crisis:  Labour MP says families can't afford London](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/06/04/12/50/PA-73608375.jpeg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
Lengthy closure consultations can leave families in limbo for months, unsure of whether to look for new school places, while staff don’t know whether to look for new jobs, according to a new report from London Councils.
The organisation, which represents the capital’s boroughs, called on the Department for Education to standardise closure procedures and ensure boroughs have the powers to make use of former school buildings as soon as possible.
Inner London has been particularly affected by closures, with eight of the 10 local authorities that have experienced the largest decreases in primary school numbers across the country coming in inner boroughs.
Earlier this year the London Assembly Economy, Culture and Skills Committee warned that serious financial and practical barriers, including the cost of childcare and housing, have played a major role in families moving out of London.
Between 2013 and 2023, London’s population of 0 to 9-year-olds fell by 99,100 as the city’s overall population grew by 506,000, prompting concerns that London, particularly the inner city, was no longer child-friendly.
Councillor Una O’Halloran, the Leader of Islington Council and London Councils Executive Member for Children and Education, told the Local Democracy Reporting Service (LDRS) that while we are unlikely to see the falling pupil numbers trend reverse anytime soon, dealing with the consequences is vital.
“Birth rate is falling – numbers are especially low in inner London,” she said. “It’s a mix of issues – the housing crisis, people’s choice not to have children and the cost of living. Brexit has also had an impact, as has the impact of remote working.
“The numbers are looking pretty bleak. We’re never going to be able to reverse that trend.
“Once you have closed a school, you are still left with a building. But we have the bureaucracy of having to go the Secretary of State and asking what the asset can be used for.
“We need to make it easier to make decisions on what we can do with closed school buildings. When we close a school, we want the powers to make sure it doesn’t remain empty for too long. If we have to do it, can we make people feel like they are a part of it?”
Closures have a significant impact on local communities, according to the report, with headteachers using “terms such as ‘traumatic’, ‘shame’, and ‘horrendous’ to describe their experiences, reflecting the considerable emotional toll”.
“While changes to school organisation are often discussed in terms of pupil numbers and finances, their human impact is equally important. Change can create uncertainty and anxiety for children, families and staff,” the foreword says.
The report does cite good practice from some boroughs about taking advantage of the empty buildings.
Hammersmith and Fulham Council has leased spare space to private and community organisations, generating over £100,000 a year for one host school.
In Bexley, meanwhile, surplus space has been used to create 122 new places for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) across nine local schools, saving an estimated £8 million by reducing reliance on costly out-of-area placements.
In Croydon, spare capacity now supports a unit helping asylum-seeking children settle into mainstream education.
Read More
However, London Councils says Department for Education (DfE) approval for such changes of use can be slow, leaving buildings standing empty in the meantime.
The DfE was contacted for comment.
summary: A new report from London Councils highlights the severe emotional and practical toll that school closures take on pupils, families, and staff due to falling birth rates and declining primary school numbers. The organisation is urging the Department for Education to standardise closure procedures and grant boroughs faster powers to repurpose empty school buildings. Factors such as the housing crisis, high cost of living, and remote working have contributed to a significant drop in London's young child population.
key_points: London Councils reports that lengthy closure consultations leave families and staff in limbo for months, with headteachers describing the process as traumatic.
Inner London has been hit hardest, with eight of the ten local authorities experiencing the largest drops in primary school numbers located in inner boroughs.
London's population of children aged 0 to 9 fell by 99,100 between 2013 and 2023, driven by issues like the housing crisis, cost of living, and falling birth rates.
London Councils is calling on the Department for Education to standardise closure procedures and allow boroughs faster powers to reuse empty school buildings.
Some boroughs have successfully repurposed surplus space, such as creating SEND places in Bexley and leasing spare space to community organisations in Hammersmith and Fulham.

title: The 7 London shows our theatre editor is most excited about this autumn
author: Andrzej Lukowski
content:
[title]
Autumn in London theatre is a time loosely delineated by the end of the rush of early to mid September shows that we’re currently experiencing (hey it’s still astronomical summer) and the encroachment of panto season, which feels like it gets earlier every year but for my purposes here ‘no Christmas shows’ is a hard and fast rule.
There will be well over 100 theatre shows opening in London during this period and if you’re looking for more of a breakdown of the biggest things coming our way this season then do check out our overview of what’s best to book for in London at the moment, or our individual monthly top ten guides.
This list, then, is purely and simply the five shows I’m personally most looking forward to seeing this autumn.
7 London theatre shows we’re most excited about in autumn 2026
Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?
I wanted to start by recommending Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? @sohoplace (Sep 21-Dec 19, pictured top), but fair warning: it looks like everyone else had got the message already – it’s sold out. At the moment it’s returns only, but yes, Gillian Anderson is absurdly great casting as acidic professor’s wife Martha in this latest outing for Edward Albee’s all-time classic.
The Standard of Living
Opening in the same week as Virginia Woolf and also looking really great (and with tickets available) is The Standard of Living by James Graham (Theatre Royal Haymarket, Sep 21-Dec 12, buy tickets here). And when I say it looks great: it should hopefully follow the rule of every James Graham play that states that the drier it sounds, the more fun it is. A drama about an economist? Yes please! To be fair bisexual Bloomsbury set mainstay John Maynard Keynes was far from just some random guy, and this production – directed by Nicholas Hytner, starring Rory Kinnear – should be another in Graham’s almost incomparable run of bangers.
![The End of the World and Hard-boiled Wonderland, Barbican Centre, 2026](https://media.timeout.com/images/106414116/image.webp) 
End of the World and Hard-Boiled Wonderland
Do you want to see an epic Japanese-language stage adaptation of Haruki Murakami’s out-there early classic Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World? I know I really, really do! And good news: a Murakami-endorsed Japanese take from French director Philippe Decouflé is coming in October (Barbican Centre, Oct 8-11), confusingly called End of the World and Hard-Boiled Wonderland. Aside from the fact that the show looks great, then it’s a relatively limited chance to see international theatre at the Barbican these days (soon there’ll be none as it shuts down in 2028 for massive upgrade works). Japanese film star Tatsuya Fujiwara (Battle Royale!) leads the cast.
![The Lives of Others, Kiera Knightley, 2026](https://media.timeout.com/images/106399702/image.webp) 
The Lives of Others
Probably now just about old enough that we should stop referring to him as a ‘wunderkind’, Robert Icke is nonetheless one of the most exciting, er, early-middle-aged directors in Britain, the cerebral yin to Jamie Lloyd’s flamboyant yang. Having already brought us a gleefully leftfield take on Romeo & Juliet earlier this year, his second show of 2026 will be an adaptation of the Oscar-winning 2006 German film The Lives of Others (Adelphi Theatre, Oct 14-Jan 9 2027, buy tickets here). It’s a very exciting prospect from a very exciting director and it’s got an amazing cast headed by Keira Knightley in her first stage role in 16 years.
Cloud 9
Britain’s greatest living playwright Caryl Churchill has just turned 88 and may or may not make any new work (I wouldn’t rule it out but she’s certainly earned retirement). But, frankly, most of her plays are too weird and too complicated to revive very often and so it is with her 1979 breakthrough Cloud 9, which hasn’t had a London production in almost 20 years. A head-spinning drama set in colonial Africa and 1979 England – with the same characters – it draws a surreal link between colonial and sexual repression and is all kinds of weird and provocative. It’s very exciting that it’s getting a major National Theatre revival (Nov 2-Jan 13 2027, buy tickets here), helmed by Dominic Cooke, who just directed the Game of Thrones play The Mad King, and who takes over at the Almeida next year.
![Ian McKellen in King Lear, Yard Theatre](https://media.timeout.com/images/106404827/image.webp) 
Lear
Finally another extravagantly sold out show but I feel I just have to stress how amazing it is that 87-year-old living legend Ian McKellen is making his stage ‘comeback’ – he famously took a tumble while playing Falstaff a couple of years back – at the ultra hip Yard Theatre in Hackney Wick. Lear (Nov 17-Jan 2 2027) is a fascinating semi-autobiographical spin on King Lear from McKellen, director Jay Miller and left-field playwright Simon Stephens. While it seems daft at this stage to suggest McKellen – the David Attenborough of stage actors – will be retiring any time soon, this is obviously something pretty special regardless.
Julius Caesar
If you want a cheeky Shakespeare recommendation that’s NOT sold out this autumn then I’d heartily recommend Julius Caesar at Shakespeare’s Globe (Nov 6-Feb 14 2027, buy tickets here). Frankly we know almost nothing about the production but it’s directed by Joe Hill-Gibbins, a cheerily provocative director who once did a production of Measure for Measure with a set entirely made of sex dolls.
Get the latest and greatest from the Big Smoke – from news and reviews to events and trends. Just follow our Time Out London WhatsApp channel.
Stay in the loop: sign up to our free Time Out London newsletter for the best of the city, straight to your inbox.
summary: The theatre editor highlights several notable London stage productions opening in autumn 2026, excluding Christmas shows and panto. The curated selection features highly anticipated revivals, literary adaptations, and star-studded casts across various iconic venues. While some major productions like Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? and Lear are already sold out, other exciting plays still have tickets available.
key_points: Gillian Anderson stars in a sold-out production of Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf? at @sohoplace.
James Graham's new play The Standard of Living runs at the Theatre Royal Haymarket, directed by Nicholas Hytner and starring Rory Kinnear.
Keira Knightley makes her return to the stage after 16 years in Robert Icke's adaptation of The Lives of Others at the Adelphi Theatre.
Caryl Churchill's 1979 breakthrough play Cloud 9 receives a major National Theatre revival directed by Dominic Cooke.
Ian McKellen stars in a semi-autobiographical spin on King Lear, titled Lear, at the Yard Theatre.

title: Victoria Beckham's florist wins High Court fight with London rival
author: Paul Keogh
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Victoria Beckham says 50th birthday party was 'best night ever' as Spice Girls reunite for starry bash](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/38/FlowerbxBeckham.jpeg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75)
![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png)
The company specialises in high-end floral displays, and counts the former Spice Girl, actress Julianne Moore, and brands like Louis Vuitton, Dior and Jimmy Choo among its customers, attracted by its reputation for style and luxury.
By 2025, it was turning over more than £4million a year, but ended up embroiled in a trademark row with London-based rival, Lukasz Gajewski, and his similarly named company, Flowers Box London Ltd.
She claimed she had lost business to the other company, as confused customers mistook it for hers due to the similarity in names and placed orders there, rather than with Flowerbx, as they intended.
![Victoria Beckham’s fashionista florist Flowerbx](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/38/FlowerbxBeckham.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
After a trial, she has now been handed victory by a judge, who ruled that Mr Gajewski's business had in fact breached her trademark, confusing customers and allowing his company to unfairly benefit from Flowerbx's hard-won reputation for quality.
Giving judgment, Recorder Amanda Michaels said that having breached the trademark by the use of "signs" comprising of the words "Flowers Box" or "Flowers Box London", Mr Gajewski's business gained an "unfair advantage" as it enabled it to "profit" from the reputation achieved by Ms Bromberg Hawkings' hard work.
The court heard during the trial that Ms Bromberg Hawkings founded Flowerbx after becoming frustrated at the lack of an online source of the sort of "elegant and modern flowers" generally used in the high-end fashion business.
"She decided to open a business to fulfil that perceived need," said the judge in her ruling.
"She said that she conceived the FLOWERBX name, which she felt would ‘sound modern, disruptive and fashion-forward'.
"Initially, she intended to create a direct-to-consumer business, but some of her contacts in the fashion business asked if the claimant could provide flowers for events such as fashion shows, or for shops or restaurants, and so the company developed a business-to-business model.
Read More
"One of the claimant’s specialities is, or was, the delivery of bouquets or arrangements of single stem varieties."
Ms Bromberg Hawkings also said that unlike many other UK florists, the claimant’s flowers are cut only after a customer places an order, minimising waste and improving freshness and quality."
![Flowerbx founder Whitney Bromberg Hawkings](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/50/FlowerbxFounder.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Ms Bromberg Hawkings’ evidence was that high-end fashion and luxury brands used FLOWERBX "for a supreme luxury experience and...for events, gifting and large-scale installations".
"She registered the trademark for Flowerbx in July 2017, claiming that her business had by then acquired a reputation for 'luxury and stylish floral design of the highest quality'."
Among its collaborations, Flowerbx worked with high-end fashion designer Emilia Wickstead for a display outside Scott's restaurant in Mayfair and in 2019 produced a large floral display for the famous London club, Annabel's.
It also collaborated with Victoria Beckham for a pop-up boutique at her flagship London store, and provided lavish floral arrangements for both Victoria and David Beckham's 50th birthday celebrations.
Flowers Box London Ltd was not incorporated until April 2019, although Mr Gajewski said he had begun trading in 2017, following in the footsteps of his florist mother.
![Lukasz Gajewski launched a similarly named company, Flowers Box London Ltd](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/45/LukaszGajewski.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Initially selling flowers via eBay, his company began to supply flowers, bouquets and plants online, targeting the luxury end of the market after it was incorporated.
The judge said Mr Gajewski's company "must have become aware of the potential for confusion" almost immediately after incorporation, as from July 2019 it received a series of messages, congratulating it for five-star online reviews actually intended for Flowerbx.
Ms Bromberg Hawkings herself became aware of the potential for confusion in late 2023 when a school bus driver told her he had bought some of her flowers, when it fact they had come from Mr Gajewski's company.
The dispute then went to the High Court, with lawyers for Flowerbx claiming that its rival had breached the trademark in its name and taken unfair reputation of its standing in the industry.
![Flowerbx display outside a Jimmy Choo store](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/05/FlowerbxChoo.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Giving her judgment, Recorder Michaels said Flowerbx had established a reputation for "luxury and stylish floral design of the highest quality" before its rival was even incorporated.
"The claimant alleged that the defendant took unfair advantage of the reputation of the mark by riding on its coat tails," she continued.
"It did not plead that the defendant had a subjective intent to take unfair advantage, so that the only possible basis for a finding of unfair advantage would be that the objective effect of the defendant’s acts is to take advantage of the mark.
"The name may have been adopted innocently, although the mark was in use and registered by the time Mr Gajewski started to use it in late 2017, and the defendant may not have intended to take unfair advantage of its reputation.
"Nevertheless, it traded with knowledge of the claimant and its business, at the latest from July 2019 when the defendant first received a Trustpilot review intended for the claimant.
![A Flowerbx display at Corinthia London Hotel](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/15/10/19/FlowerbxCorinthia.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
"That was reinforced by Mr Gajewski’s periodic visits to the claimant’s website and his subscription to the claimant’s marketing emails.
"I am satisfied that the defendant took unfair advantage of the distinctive character or repute of the mark, as it gave the defendant an advantage which was unfair because it enabled the defendant to profit from the reputation achieved by the claimant’s hard work and marketing efforts."
The question of how much in damages Flowers Box London Ltd has to pay Ms Bromberg Hawkings' company will be decided at another court hearing at a later date.
summary: High-end florist Flowerbx, founded by Whitney Bromberg Hawkings, has won a High Court trademark battle against London rival Lukasz Gajewski and his company, Flowers Box London Ltd. A judge ruled that the rival business breached Flowerbx's trademark and unfairly profited from its reputation by causing customer confusion. The question of damages will be determined at a future court hearing.
key_points: Flowerbx counts high-profile clients like Victoria Beckham, Louis Vuitton, and Dior among its customers.
By 2025, Flowerbx was turning over more than £4 million a year and registered its trademark in July 2017.
Recorder Amanda Michaels ruled that Flowers Box London Ltd breached the trademark and gained an unfair advantage through customer confusion.
The rival company became aware of potential confusion as early as July 2019 after receiving online reviews intended for Flowerbx.
A future court hearing will decide how much in damages Flowers Box London Ltd must pay to Flowerbx.

title: What's the story? Not a single London gig among Oasis' 38 tour dates
author: Holly Bishop
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
The iconic Britpop act confirmed a 38-date live tour from May to September next year with dates in the UK, Europe and America.
The UK shows are made up of five dates in Glasgow, 11 dates in Manchester and four at Knebworth, 30 years after they played historic two nights at the Hertfordshire venue in 1996.
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/14/17/01M2G8EQ1S9YWM9AT5VFBJTKX7.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
But London fans are disappointed that no specific dates in the capital have been announced.
But the nearest gig for Londoners this time round is well beyond the boundaries of the M25 in Knebworth, a 20 to 40 minute journey by train from King's Cross or St Pancras International.
Alternatively, it is a 30-mile drive from central London expected to take hours on concert day.
Fans in the capital have been taken aback by the lack of London shows, with some calling the choice a “snub”.
![The rock group Oasis have had a string of notable hits (PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2024/08/25/21/0e31eba4e7dc217e0e149ffc6999fc03Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzI0NzAzNDA5-2.1037734.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
"You saw everyone in London wearing bucket hats and Adidas tops last year, it was such a good vibe. It feels like a missed opportunity not to do it all over again,” said one disappointed fan.
"London is so much better setup for this than anywhere else. Everyone who was at Knebworth the first time said the sound was rubbish!,” they added.
“Only Manchester? No London? It’s gonna be even harder to get a ticket than last year,” said another, whilst a fourth added: “Nothing in London, meh.”
Another fan said: “It’s really exciting that Oasis are back next year. I saw them at Wembley Stadium two years ago and it was one of the best nights of my life. I'm just gutted they’re not coming back to the capital, it does feel like a bit of a snub.”
However, others praised the decision to leave the capital off of the list. “They don't owe nothing to London, they were made in the North, by the North. Londoners get to see any act they want to at the O2 or Wembley, can't they make the trip up to Manchester once in a while?
“Why not support local economies in the UK outside one of the richest cities in the world?”
"You lot get everything, so shush," said another user in response to a complaining fan from the capital.
“After a period of reflection “The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force In Recent British History” has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people.
Read More
“Come witness the fitness. It shall be a sight to behold,” the band said.
![An Oasis fan holds a banner and poses for a photo on Wembley Way (Lucy North/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2025/10/16/08/7eb27957420704d75a11f1be8abe9cceY29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzYwNjg1MjIx-2.81097145.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)

title: London musical run cancelled after Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey drop out | LBC
author: Flaminia Luck
content:
London musical run cancelled after Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey drop out
A revival of the musical 'Sunday in the Park with George' has been officially cancelled after both Wicked stars pulled out.
A revival of the musical 'Sunday in the Park with George' has been officially cancelled after both Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey pulled out.
Listen to this article
The Wicked stars were due to lead the production at the Barbican theatre in London next year.
Following Grande's departure, Bailey announced he would also withdraw from the play, saying: âAri is one of my dearest friends, and my support for her is unwavering.â
However, Empire Street Productions says it "will retain the rights" of the Stephen Sondheim musical with plans to present it in 2028.
Grande announced she would be stepping back from public life following the conclusion of her 'Eternal Sunshine' tour afterÂ what her team called "endless, ongoing scrutiny."
The US pop star performed the final night of a 10-night sold out residency at the O2 earlier this month and wept as she thanked fans for being âby her sideâ.
While Grande may have stepped back from public life, she popped up in a trailer for the latest film in the 'Meet the Fockers' franchise.
The music megastar plays the new fiancÃ©e of the son of Ben Stiller's character Greg.
Grande has been in the public eye since breaking out as a child star in her teens with a role in the Disney drama Victorious. She has gone on to release eight albums since 2013.
She won three Grammy awards during her successful music career, which took off in 2013 after the release of her debut album, Yours Truly.
She was also nominated for an Oscar for her role as Glinda in the big screen adaptation of Wicked.
Her personal and often tumultuous life has also been a consistent source of news gossip and she was married to Dalton Gomez, an estate agent, from 2020 to 2023. She was also briefly engaged to comedian Pete Davidson and had a long-term relationship with singer Mac Miller, who died of an overdose in 2018.
The accidental drug overdose happened just over a year after the Manchester Arena bombing at Grande's concert, which killed 22 people and injured dozens more.
Grande is currently dating her ex-boyfriend Ricky Alvarez whom she dated back in 2014.
Alvarez, 35, is a dancer and choreographer from San Diego who has worked with Grande and has appeared in multiple music videos and concerts.
Alvarez was referenced in Grandeâs 2018 song 'thank u, next', and is thought to be the alleged inspiration for her hit song 'Into You'.
summary: A London revival of the musical 'Sunday in the Park with George' at the Barbican theatre has been cancelled after lead actors Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey withdrew from the production. Grande's departure follows her team's announcement that she is stepping back from public life after her 'Eternal Sunshine' tour due to ongoing scrutiny. Empire Street Productions retains the rights to the Stephen Sondheim musical and plans to stage it in 2028.
key_points: A revival of 'Sunday in the Park with George' at the Barbican theatre has been cancelled.
Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey both withdrew from leading the production.
Empire Street Productions plans to present the musical in 2028.
Grande is stepping back from public life following the conclusion of her 'Eternal Sunshine' tour.

title: East London food redistribution warehouse opens in Barking
author: Wendy Hurrell; Jess Warren
content:
![A group of people stand in a row and cheer as colourful confetti falls around them.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/ef39/live/fe214220-adbe-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
The hub redistributes food that would have otherwise gone to waste
- Published
A food redistribution hub that aims to deliver up to 10 tonnes of food to charities and food banks each week has opened in east London.
The Big Heart Food Hub in Barking will support more than 20 local organisations that work directly with residents struggling with the cost of living.
Most of the food will be unsold items that would otherwise have gone to waste, and will feed an estimated 7,000 residents each week.
Nathan Grady, charity food coordinator, said: "We are statistically the poorest borough in London and we recognise that there's a big need. People are missing meals - children are missing meals."
'A stepping stone'
The hub is a partnership between Barking and Dagenham Council, The Kindness Offensive, Food for All, Felix, City Harvest and Kingsley Hall.
Felix, a food redistribution charity, collects surplus food from shops and other providers so that it is not thrown away or incinerated.
It is given to local organisations, food banks, soup kitchens and schools, said David Goodfellow, one of the managers at Big Heart and a founder of The Kindness Offensive.
"They are the ones who are on the front line and they don't have the resources to be able to feed all the people that are coming to their doors," he said.
"We are a stepping stone, a middle ground between some of the big suppliers and some of the community-facing groups, to give them the supplies that they need.
"There's a lot of people who are hungry."
![A young man in a high-visibility vest and cap stands in a warehouse with crates of food behind him.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/8fcc/live/08bc34a0-add4-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
Volunteer Kamran Ali said it was "a good feeling" to help people in need
Sana Sajid is one of the people who will be receiving food from the Big Heart Food Hub to redistribute.
She and her husband run a food club at Darul Ummah Goresbrook community centre for people that are struggling financially.
"If we can help them with food, it means that they will have more money to pay their bills," she said. "It makes a big difference."
According to the Trust for London, external, food insecurity has increased by 23% from 2022/23 to 2024/25.
![An aerial view of four people working in a food distribution warehouse.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1504/cpsprodpb/bbe5/live/7ea04260-add4-11f1-a40e-b70f4378d974.jpg)
Redistributed food is given to local organisations, food banks, soup kitchens and schools
Saima Ashraf, deputy leader of Barking and Dagenham Council, said the focus was on delivering "surplus good food" through a partnership approach.
"It's sad that we have to use food banks, however it is also sad that a lot of food is being thrown away. Surplus good food - not rotten food - is going to residents and families that deserve it," she said.
The partnership hopes that in the future, Big Heart will also offer volunteering programmes, training and development opportunities.
"We don't want it just to be food distribution," said Nathan Grady, charity food coordinator.
He said: "We want to create jobs out of it and teach people how to cook with the food that they get.
"So when they come to a food bank they're not like: 'What's the celeriac? What do I do with it?'"

summary: A new food redistribution hub called the Big Heart Food Hub has opened in Barking, east London, to supply charities and food banks with surplus food. The facility aims to deliver up to 10 tonnes of unsold food weekly to support an estimated 7,000 residents struggling with the cost of living. Developed through a partnership including Barking and Dagenham Council and various charities, the hub acts as a middle ground to help local organizations feed those in need.
key_points: The Big Heart Food Hub in Barking aims to deliver up to 10 tonnes of food weekly to support over 20 local organisations.
The facility redistributes mostly unsold surplus food that would otherwise go to waste to feed an estimated 7,000 residents each week.
The hub is a partnership involving Barking and Dagenham Council, The Kindness Offensive, Food for All, Felix, City Harvest, and Kingsley Hall.
Future plans for the hub include offering volunteering programmes, job creation, and cooking training for residents.

title: Tube strike warning after RMT passes new walkout mandate in four-day week row
author: Nicholas Cecil
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![WEST END FINAL](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/newsletters/newsletter_we_final_embed_desktop.png) “With our capital city vital to the growth of the whole UK, more strikes would cripple that.” ![Conservative MP Richard Holden (Liam McBurney/PA)](https://static.standard.co.uk/2024/10/22/00/7f023d967e9a5571b5b7dfe4bb50b801Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzI5NjA2NjA4-2.71634294.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) He warned London Mayor Lord Sadiq Khan against making concessions to the RMT, arguing the union would just “keep striking for more, despite having some of the best paid, pensioned, and secure jobs in the country”. He spoke out after the RMT passed a new strike mandate earlier in the summer to carry on its industrial action. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/04/24/13/2272404284.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) The overall number of drivers who sent back ballots was 134 lower than in February when 1,801 were eligible to vote compared to 1,719 in the most recent mandate renewal. On taking industrial action short of strikes, 978 drivers backed the move, or 93% of the 1,050 who took part in the August ballot, with 71 against. The RMT said: “Both of the above results exceed the required thresholds and the National Executive Committee has wholeheartedly congratulated members on delivering a ballot mandate for strike action and action short of a strike.” Read More But the RMT has branded the changes as a “fake” four-day week, arguing it was compressing five days of work into four. It has cited concerns over the impact on drivers who do not want to accept the new arrangements, as well as on driver fatigue and late notice of shifts. ![

Stacked Tube trains at Upminster rail depot during the RMT walkout in April

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/04/22/06/2272383602.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) But the RMT’s position has been hugely undermined by the Aslef train drivers’ union fully backing the reforms and praising the four-day week as the “biggest improvement in working conditions for Underground train drivers in decades”. Aslef stressed Tube drivers would get “working conditions that are as good as, or better than, those on any mainline train company”, including an extra 35 days away from work a year, average weekly rostered hours reducing to 34 from a current average of 36, and a third rest day every week so more time at home and less time travelling to and from work.
summary: The RMT union has secured a new walkout mandate amid a dispute over a four-day working week for London Underground drivers. While the RMT criticized the changes as compressed hours raising fatigue and shift concerns, the rival Aslef union fully backed the reforms. Conservative MP Richard Holden has warned London Mayor Sadiq Khan against making concessions to the RMT.
key_points: The RMT passed a new strike mandate following an August ballot that exceeded required thresholds.
The RMT opposes the new arrangements, branding them a 'fake' four-day week that compresses five days of work into four and raises fatigue concerns.
The Aslef train drivers' union fully backed the reforms, praising them as a major improvement in working conditions.
Conservative MP Richard Holden warned London Mayor Sadiq Khan against making concessions to the RMT.

title: London musical cancelled after Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey pull out
author: Emma Saunders
content:
![Jonathan Bailey, wearing a white open-necked shirt, and Ariana Grande in a black top and pearl stud earrings, at a Q&A on the film Wicked: For Good in Los Angeles. They are both laughing.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/90c4/live/cf57afc0-b03d-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
- Published
The upcoming London revival of Sunday In The Park With George has been cancelled after A-listers Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey dropped out.
The Wicked stars had been due to reunite on stage in the Stephen Sondheim show at the Barbican next year.
Last month, Grande announced she was pulling out of the musical as part of her decision to take a break from the spotlight after completing her Eternal Sunshine Tour.
Earlier this month, Bailey also revealed he was withdrawing from the show. Production company Empire Street Productions initially said it would continue as planned but on Monday announced the musical would no longer be staged in 2027.
Show may run in 2028
A statement from the company said: "The planned 2027 production of Sunday in the Park with George at the Barbican will no longer proceed as scheduled.
"Empire Street Productions will retain the rights with a view to presenting the production in 2028. Further details will be announced in due course."
US composer Sondheim and playwright James Lapine created the original musical, which debuted on Broadway in 1984.
Sunday in the Park with George was inspired by French painter Georges Seurat's A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte, in which a fictional version of the artist is consumed by his work.
![Ariana Grance in a black off the shoulder dress at this year's Golden Globe awards](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/f4d1/live/f306c090-b034-11f1-9ae0-e316eeb4632d.jpg)
Grande and Bailey played Glinda and Fiyero in the film adaptation of Wicked and its sequel, Wicked: For Good.
Grande's publicist announced in August that the singer and actress would be "taking a step back from visibility" after her recent tour ended.
A representative for the US star told People magazine that she "will be taking a step back from visibility" when the tour ends, after her appearances led to "endless, ongoing public scrutiny".
Grande's physical appearance and health have been a topic of speculation in recent years.
She later told fans at a Chicago concert: "The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing. It is something that I had decided to plan... quietly, a long time ago."
"I heard my fans were worried negativity was ruining things for me but... that could not be more than the opposite.
"Boundaries need to be set, human beings do need a break sometimes."
When Bailey pulled out of Sunday in the Park with George at the beginning of September, he voiced support for its director Marianne Elliott, external and said: "I so look forward to seeing what the team, and the two actors who will now take on these roles, will create with it," he continued.
"I wish the very best to the entire company. I will be cheering them on as they continue with this production."
Bailey previously collaborated with Elliot on the play Cock and Sondheim's musical Company in the West End.
summary: The planned London revival of the musical Sunday In The Park With George at the Barbican has been cancelled for 2027 after lead actors Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey withdrew from the production. Grande pulled out to take a break from the spotlight following her tour, while Bailey withdrew earlier this month. Production company Empire Street Productions stated it still holds the rights and aims to stage the production in 2028.
key_points: The 2027 London revival of Sunday In The Park With George at the Barbican has been cancelled.
Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey withdrew from the Stephen Sondheim musical after previously starring together in Wicked.
Grande pulled out as part of a planned break from the spotlight following her Eternal Sunshine Tour.
Empire Street Productions retains the rights and hopes to present the show in 2028.

title: Londoner warns reckless e-bike riders are a 'danger' for cyclists
author: Tom Edwards
content:
![A woman sits in front of a plant in her kitchen](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/04b6/live/cd0ecc00-ab6d-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Morwenna Hughes had to have a plate and six screws into her left arm after the accident
- Published
Cyclists say recklessly ridden and illegally souped up e-bikes have become a danger to them on the capital's bike lanes and roads.
Morwenna Hughes was riding on a conventional bicycle on a busy, two-way cycle lane in Hammersmith when an e-bike rider cut her up and knocked her off in a hit and run.
Her face was smashed and she may not regain full mobility in her left arm after it was shattered in the crash.
Hughes is calling for registration for e-bikes, a re-evaluation of two-way bike lanes and says pay per minute rentals also encourage reckless behaviour such as jumping red lights.
![A woman with bruised face and arm in plaster](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1280/cpsprodpb/7902/live/1bf7fe80-ab65-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Hughes said the accident happened so fast that she did not see what kind e-bike it was
The collision happened along King Street's two-way cycle lane on 16 June.
Hughes said the incident happened so fast that she was not sure what kind of e-bike she was hit by.
"When I got to A&E, they tried to realign my arm and couldn't," she said.
"And then when I went back a couple of days later, they told me that I'd shattered the bone and I would need to have plate and six screws in my arm. So I had the operation.
"Obviously the scar's still there and I'm hoping that will that will fade over time. I've been told it's probably four months of physio, and I probably won't get the full recovery for up to a year, but they're saying that it may be that I only get 70% of my movement back."
Hughes has been a cyclist in London for 25 years but collision has shaken her confidence to the point where she is unsure if she will cycle again.
"I'm a huge fan of cycling and I'm an advocate for getting people on bikes.
"But this has really shaken my confidence both as a cyclist but also as a pedestrian. And just being even a pedestrian in busy areas where there's e-bikes around, I feel very anxious."
She added: "Up until maybe a year ago, cars always felt like the biggest danger to me. But I think in the last year, I definitely feel that recklessly driven e-bikes are a far bigger danger to cyclists.
"And it feels like it is just increasing. So I do feel like it has got progressively worse over the last few months to the point now where in some parts of my commute, I feel like you're almost outnumbered by e-bikes."
![A woman is lying on the pavement in pain, a bike is infront of her.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1440/cpsprodpb/758e/live/70a6ff20-adbe-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.png)
Jane Ouartsi was left with life-changing injuries after being hit by a Lime bike but has not received any compensation
E-bikes are getting more and more popular in the capital. They are convenient, easy to use and have zero emissions.
But injuries to both pedestrians and the riders have been a concern. E-bikes are available to hire via operators such as Lime, Forest and Voi or are available to buy privately.
Hospitals have reported an increase in injuries to both riders and pedestrians.
Legal e-bikes can only go 15.5mph but many are illegally tampered with or "chipped" to go much faster and should technically be classed as motorbikes.
As first reported on BBC London, Jane Ouartsi was hit by a minor riding a Lime bike.
The impact was very serious and long lasting. She suffered a broken femur, a fractured collar bone and two spinal fractures requiring three operations.
She had to spend 36 days in hospital.
The police did not take action against the boy and there has been no compensation from Lime.
Since BBC London reported the incident, Lime has still not been in contact with Jane or her family.
![Two Lime bike riders overtake a cyclist](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/9469/live/ebaa2b00-adc0-11f1-ac2c-11e32c6809db.jpg)
The collision took place in this two-way bike lane in Hammersmith
Hughes also believes the model for hire bikes needs to be changed.
"If people are renting Lime bikes or Forest bikes, they're paying by the minute," she said.
"I understand they might want to get to their destination as quickly as possible but there are so many people cycling recklessly and because they are unaccountable for their reckless cycling."
![Close up of a woman with blonde hair on the right hand side, head tilting to her left. She has a nose stud and fine silver earring in. The background is blurred.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/9677/live/d869e6c0-ab6d-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Hughes says two-way cycle lanes need to be re-evaluated especially when both kinds of bikes are on them
Tom Fyans is from the London Cycling Campaign.
He says street illegal "fake" e-bikes that retain power over 15.5mph and do not need pedalling have no place on London's streets.
"Legal ebikes help get loads more people cycle who never would have otherwise - with all the benefits to health, climate, pollution and yes reducing road danger these bring.
"But we need to tackle the illegal bikes and ensure every road user, cyclist or not, obeys the Highway Code, to keep us all safe."
![Two riders in a bike lane in King Street, Hammersmith](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/348f/live/fa3ace40-adc0-11f1-ac2c-11e32c6809db.jpg)
Two-way cycle lanes need to be reconsidered, according to Hughes
Hughes also believes more action should be taken to regulate e-bike use and where they can be used.
"Registration is key. I know it would be really difficult to implement it, but I think that this has to be done.
"We should also look at the safety of two-way bike lanes... they're fundamentally flawed once you've got e-bikes in the mix. I think that it means that normal road bikes are far more vulnerable."
She said she also wanted to see "more resources within the police for stopping people who are driving recklessly and especially people who are driving private e-bikes over the speed limit".
![A woman is sitting with her arm in a cast. She has bruising on around her right eye and has a pink cast on her left forearm. She is sat down in a hospital room, wearing a pinstripe hospital gown.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/3f0a/live/0bdf5bb0-ab65-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Hughes may not gain full mobility in her left arm
City Hall and the government have no plans to introduce registration for e-bikes but the dockless e-bike operator Forest has introduced plates on 500 of its bikes in Richmond to try and stop reckless riding.
The Metropolitan Police has been carrying out operations to crack down on illegally souped up e-bikes.
Hammersmith and Fulham council which owns the bike lane has been approached for comment.
Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook, external, X, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk, external
summary: London cyclists and pedestrians are warning that recklessly driven and illegally modified e-bikes have become a major danger in the capital's bike lanes and roads. Morwenna Hughes, a cyclist of 25 years, suffered a shattered arm and facial injuries in a hit-and-run collision with an e-bike in Hammersmith. In response to increasing accidents and severe injuries, victims and cycling advocates are calling for better enforcement, e-bike registration, and a re-evaluation of two-way cycle lanes.
key_points: Morwenna Hughes sustained severe arm and facial injuries after being knocked off her conventional bicycle by an e-bike in a hit-and-run incident in Hammersmith.
Legal e-bikes are restricted to 15.5mph, but many are illegally tampered with to travel much faster.
Hughes is calling for e-bike registration, more police resources to stop reckless riding, and a re-evaluation of two-way cycle lanes.
Pay-per-minute hire models are said to encourage reckless behaviors such as jumping red lights.
While City Hall and the government currently have no plans to introduce e-bike registration, some operators and police are testing or implementing targeted measures.

title: Seething Lane: A Samuel Pepys Mystery by Jack Jewers - The Reviews Hub
author: The Reviews Hub
content:
When it comes to historical fiction, timing is everything. For his second novel, Jack Jewers returns to the 17th century and it’s hard to think of a better period in which to create drama. Just a couple of generations’ reach from Shakespeare, and a few years after the Great Fire of London, not to mention the restoration of Charles II to the throne, Jewers’ novel, Seething Lane, is set in 1670 and bears witness to these seismic changes through its principal character, diarist Samuel Pepys.
From the start, Jewers makes it clear that this Samuel Pepys is a work of imagination: many of the facts of his life are present in the novel, but Jewers allows creative licence to take hold. As we join Pepys in the opening scenes, we find him acting as an administrator for the Order of the Royal Oak, a secret organisation that has Pepys spying on a preacher who seems to threaten the stability of the Crown. Returning home to his offices in Seething Lane, Pepys is intercepted by a young man who begs to have a word with him. He is too busy, and distracted, to respond.
When Henry Fitzwilliam, an aristocrat with direct links to Charles II’s eldest son, is found dead, Pepys’ keenly observant eye is recruited to find the killer. A shocking connection between Fitzwilliam and the young man at Pepys’ office door soon becomes apparent. As London experiences its worst winter in decades, Pepys’ investigation takes him from the Palace to the intimacy of backstage theatre life, as Charles II’s mistress, Nell Gwyn, returns to the stage.
Jewers successfully recreates a world captured in the pages of Samuel Pepys’ diaries. While no-one misses Cromwell, there is still an insistence on old values and privileges that chafe against an incoming 18th-century modernity. Seething Lane doesn’t heave under the weight of history; it bustles with life: urban grime and Restoration glamour. Jewers resists the temptation to overwrite 17th-century dialogue: the stuffiness sometimes associated with historical fiction doesn’t apply here. Someone is even called a “pillock” (and with good reason). Jewers’ experience as a filmmaker keeps the plot moving and the characters engaging.
While Pepys, as a literary character, remains elusive and a touch bland as a detective, Jewers’ best work is in his supporting cast. The world of Drury Lane Theatre is beautifully drawn: playwright Aphra Behn dominates the page wherever she appears. Nell Gwyn, the larger-than-life actress who steals the heart of the monarch, is an absolute riot. Jewers imagines her as a Cockney girl whose street-smarts save the day on more than one occasion. The reader is forgiven if they fall in love with her too.
What is really impressive is how Jewers combines scholarship with readability. He balances the wealth of research it takes to write such a novel with a page-turning murder mystery. But after the mystery is unravelled, what remains with the reader is the vibrant energy of the world that Jewers so clearly adores.
Seething Lane is published by Moonflower Books at £18.99 and is out now
summary: Jack Jewers' historical novel "Seething Lane" is set in 1670 London and features a fictionalized version of diarist Samuel Pepys as a detective. After dismissing a young man at his office, Pepys is tasked with investigating the murder of aristocrat Henry Fitzwilliam, whose death links back to that same young man. The investigation leads Pepys through a harsh winter from the Royal Palace to the backstage world of theatre involving figures like Nell Gwyn and Aphra Behn.
key_points: The novel is set in 1670 and uses historical figure Samuel Pepys as its main character and investigator.
Pepys is tasked with finding the killer of aristocrat Henry Fitzwilliam, uncovering a connection to a young man he previously ignored.
The story blends historical research with a murder mystery, moving from the Palace to Drury Lane Theatre.
Supporting characters like playwright Aphra Behn and actress Nell Gwyn are standout figures in the novel.
"Seething Lane" is published by Moonflower Books at £18.99 and is available now.

title: Teenager who travelled over 150 miles to kill alleged stalker admits murder
author: Georgia Bates
content:
Teenager who travelled from Yorkshire to London to kill alleged stalker admits murder
A teenager who purchased a knife and travelled more than 150 miles to confront and fatally stab a man his family had accused of stalking has admitted murder.
Afghan refugee Sulaiman Tajzai, 18, pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey on Friday to the murder of 26-year-old Farmanullah Sherzad, the Metropolitan Police said.
Tajzai, of Leeds, also admitted a charge of possession of a bladed article and is due to be sentenced at the same court on September 18.
Jurors previously heard that on March 27, Tajzai bought the weapon from a shop near his home in Leeds and travelled to the victim’s address in Westminster in London, that same day.
It was heard he attacked and repeatedly stabbed Mr Sherzad, who had been the subject of multiple complaints by family members.
Officers were called to reports of a stabbing on Abbey Orchard Street shortly before 10.15pm. Mr Sherzad suffered multiple stab wounds and died from his injuries.
Tajzai was caught on CCTV arriving at London’s King’s Cross station and was tracked on CCTV walking across London before reaching Mr Sherzad’s home.
The victim left work at 10pm and cycled home where Tajzai was waiting for him, the trial was told.
CCTV footage shows there was a scuffle near Mr Sherzad’s house, and that he ran “screaming for his life” as Tajzai attacked him, Lisa Wilding KC said.
Tajzai ran away from the scene and tried to catch a train back to Leeds from King’s Cross station, however missed it and got onto another one just after 6am the following day.
He was arrested at his cousin’s house in Leeds on March 29 and police officers searched the address, seizing multiple items belonging to him including a pair of blood-stained trainers.
![Afghan refugee Sulaiman Tajzai, 18, (right) pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey on Friday to the murder of 26-year-old Farmanullah Sherzad (left) the Metropolitan Police said.](<https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/jpim-static/image/2026/09/13/11/17/1200-x-630-(4).png?trim=0,0,199,0&width=640&quality=65>)
![placeholder image](https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/img/placeholder.jpg)
The alleged animosity against Mr Sherzad was said to have dated back to the autumn of 2025.
The prosecutor said there was a clear “pre-existing connection” between the defendant’s cousin’s wife and Mr Sherzad which had “turned sour”.
The cousin and his wife had reported him to police in Leeds in September last year, showing an officer an image of the victim and text messages in Arabic.
When spoken to privately, the wife deleted the texts, refused to sign a statement and left the police station.
Last October 3, police officers attended the couple’s home in Leeds and found Mr Sherzad sitting on the floor with his wrists tied together with fabric and no shoes on, jurors heard.
Mr Sherzad was arrested on suspicion of stalking and trespass with intent to commit a sexual offence, the court heard.
However, he went on to claim to be in a relationship with the wife, saying he had come to Leeds to visit after she had invited him on social media platform Snapchat.
Following his release, the defendant’s cousin and his wife contacted the police multiple times and were later told there would be “no further action” against Mr Sherzad.
CCTV footage revealed Tajzai had travelled to London in the weeks before the attack to scope out Mr Sherzad’s home address and where he worked, the police said.
In a statement issued after Tajzai pleaded guilty, Detective Chief Inspector Wayne Jolley, who led the investigation, said: “This is a devastating case in which a young man lost his life after being subjected to a brutal and senseless act of violence.
“No family should have to endure the pain of losing a loved one in such circumstances.”
summary: Eighteen-year-old Sulaiman Tajzai pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey to the murder of 26-year-old Farmanullah Sherzad. Tajzai traveled more than 150 miles from Leeds to London after purchasing a knife to confront the victim, whose alleged stalking had been the subject of complaints by the defendant's family. Following the fatal stabbing on Abbey Orchard Street, Tajzai fled back to Leeds, where he was arrested by police two days later.
key_points: Sulaiman Tajzai, 18, pleaded guilty to the murder of 26-year-old Farmanullah Sherzad and possession of a bladed article.
Tajzai bought a knife in Leeds and travelled over 150 miles to Westminster, London, to attack the victim.
The defendant's family had previously made multiple complaints accusing the victim of stalking.
CCTV footage tracked Tajzai traveling to London, scoping out the location, and fleeing the scene after the attack.
Tajzai was arrested at his cousin's house in Leeds on March 29 and is scheduled to be sentenced on September 18.

title: US secretly flew diplomat out of UK after indecent image allegations – reports
author: Christopher McKeon
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/12/23/2a95ab04a0f0d4f7cded292e141e9586Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzg5MzM5MjMx-2.78276019.jpg?crop=8:5,smart&quality=75&auto=webp&width=1000)
